_comment: Committed lock for both test262 runners. corpus must match PINNED_COMMIT. language/builtins are pass-count floors. negAcceptExact is the exact accepted-negative count and must match test262-neg-accepts.json; the language runner also compares every path, so one-for-one swaps fail. Refresh only for a corpus bump or reviewed parser change. fix/wrong-values-2 (2026-08-27): refreshed both floors; Fail:0 confirmed on both runners. language DROPS 3003->2976 (not a straight trade of the 29 WRONG-VALUE closures; see below): closing comma/instanceof/break/continue's root cause (src/compile/emit.js's bare-identifier-read fallback, which used to blindly guess `local.get $name` for ANY unresolved name; silently correct only when the guess's value went unused and dead-code elimination happened to drop it) now rejects an unresolved read UNCONDITIONALLY. A reachability gate was added on top (src/compile/emit.js: emitBlockBody's statement loop AND the ';' statement-list emitter both now stop walking a list once isTerminator() proves an unconditional return/throw/break/continue precedes; src/type.js's existing predicate, reused not reinvented) so code textually after such a statement, which real JS never evaluates either, is skipped instead of wrongly rejected; this alone recovered part of the initial 29-test drop (2974->2976). Two DEEPER, narrower classes of unreachability remain unrecovered, confirmed via a baseline-worktree A/B diff (not a guess): (1) an if/while CONDITION expression that unconditionally throws before yielding true/false (test262 Sputnik idiom: `if ((function(){throw 1})()) abracadabra`; S12.5_A3.js, S12.6.2_A9.js, S12.6.1_A9.js and siblings), proving THIS needs general 'does this expression subtree always throw' analysis, not a statement-list scan; (2) sloppy-mode assignment to an undeclared name (S13_A15_T3.js's `THE_ANSWER="..."` top-level bare assignment, later read); jz has NO general implicit-global write-legalization (a pre-existing, deliberately-scoped-out gap; src/prepare/index.js's for-in target-binder carries its own comment explaining why a GENERAL version was never built: it would also have to loosen undeclared READS, which the whole point of this fix line keeps closed); these files passed in baseline only via the SAME accidental drop-the-guessed-read mechanism as the fixed entries, never on a sound basis. Both are out of reach in the time available without risking a repeat of this same pass's own 'u+' regression (see src/compile/emit.js's own comment on that revert); named and left, not silently reduced. Fail:0 is the load-bearing invariant, not the raw pass count, per STABILITY.md's own priority ("any unlisted silent wrong value is release-blocking"). builtins RISES 853->858 (unaffected by the reachability gate; several ToPrimitive/reflection fixes landing exact, zero regressions, Fail:0 before and after). fix/parser-residuals (2026-08-29): negAcceptExact 137->81 across several early-error additions (see test262-neg-accepts.json families and STABILITY.md's residual count); language/builtins floors untouched (rejection-only changes, verified Fail:0 and Pass unchanged at 2976/858 before and after each addition). One native-sound rule (strict-mode `for (let in o)` as a for-in/of target) was reverted despite closing a ledger file: the self-compiled kernel accepts it regardless of the native result, a confirmed self-host-only divergence (see early-errors.js's own NOTE at the for-in/of head handler) — left reverted rather than shipping a native/kernel mismatch. fix/parser-residuals-2: negAcceptExact 81->74 by restoring expression-slot distinctions erased in jessie's shared AST shapes (call-vs-array comma lists, grouping-vs-statement lists, debugger statement context, and block-vs-object left edges); language/builtins floors unchanged, Fail:0 and Pass:2976 confirmed by the full language leg. The for-header follow-up closes 13 more paths (74->61) by source-validating classic semicolon arity, top-level in/of and lexical-binding shape, including the ConditionalExpression [+In] middle-arm exception, while walking classic clauses as expressions rather than a shared StatementList; the full language leg again held Pass:2976/Fail:0. Restricted-boundary validation then closes 4 paths (61->57): postfix update crossing a LineTerminator must have a valid prefix fallback, `do {}` admits no intervening empty statement before `while`, and lone CR is normalized to LF for subscript's line-comment terminator; a broader `else` boundary attempt was discarded after the corpus exposed valid property-name and dangling-else/function-expression counterexamples. Pass:2976/Fail:0 remains exact. Adjacent quote-token validation closes the two legacy four-quote string paths (57->55) while preserving semicolon, operator, comma, newline-ASI, and sibling-block boundaries; the full corpus remains Pass:2976/Fail:0. Async contextual-boundary validation closes the 2-path async-arrow family plus the object-method LineTerminator path (55->52): exact `async` must remain same-line with formals/property names and escaped `async` cannot introduce an arrow. A generic call-expression-as-formals rule was narrowed after 12 valid StatementList block/class/function + arrow siblings proved the merged AST shape is shared; the corrected corpus is Pass:2976/Fail:0. Class source/AST correlation closes 20 modifier and element-boundary paths (52->32): static-async methods regain async/static validation, and same-line fields require a real separator. The first boundary draft rejected 80 valid escaped method-name/auto-accessor files; escaped OWN keys and `accessor name` pairs are now explicit exemptions, after which the full corpus returns to Pass:2976/Fail:0. Four module-goal-only class-name paths remain. Assignment-pattern source boundaries close the final 6 destructuring-cover paths (32->26): a final rest comma remains valid in literals but is rejected when the same cover node is the direct target of assignment/for-in/for-of. Pass:2976/Fail:0 remains exact. Semicolon-sensitive export/literal boundaries close 5 module-context paths (26->21), while exported function/class declarations remain free to end at their closing brace. Pass:2976/Fail:0 remains exact; the three remaining module-family paths require an external Script/Module goal the compile API does not carry. Strict source correlation closes the 10 nested Directive-Prologue escape paths plus root-strict `for (let in obj)` (21->10): an own strict directive validates every raw prologue string, while sloppy functions/blocks/siblings stay legal; the source scanner avoids the prior kernel-only for-target divergence. Pass:2976/Fail:0 remains exact. v1 source-goal closure: explicit sourceType script/module validation rejects the final 8 goal-dependent paths, and source-aware if/else boundary checks reject the final 2 ASI paths; negAcceptExact 10->0 with Pass:2976/Fail:0 unchanged.
